_readme: Copy this file to config.json and edit it. config.json is git-ignored, so your setup stays yours.
Monitor IDs: run  .\switch.ps1 -DryRun  (it lists every monitor it can see before it complains about this template),
or   .\MultiMonitorTool.exe /scomma monitors.csv  and read the 'Short Monitor ID' column.
Use the Short Monitor ID (e.g. AOC2401), the serial number, or the \\.\DISPLAYn name. Never a bare number:
to MultiMonitorTool '2' means \\.\DISPLAY2, and Windows renumbers those on driver installs and hot-plugs.
Audio: { "monitor": ID } picks the audio that belongs to that monitor (HDMI/DP audio, or headphones in its jack).
.\switch.ps1 -ListAudio shows every active playback device and which monitor it belongs to.
Other forms: { "id": ... } or { "topology": ... } from that listing, or { "name": ... } as a last resort
(Windows resets device names on driver installs).
_place_values: keep = preserve minimized/maximized/normal | normal | max | min | left | right (half of the destination work area)

rules._comment: example: Discord maximized on a side monitor when at the desk. Delete or edit.
example: WhatsApp on the right half of a side monitor
example: File Explorer windows un-maximized on the desk monitor

_rule_keys: when: desk|couch|omit for both. match: any of process (exe name), class, title (substring); all given must match. monitor: optional, default = new primary. place: optional.
